descriptionChirho: To fall to the ground, especially in reverence, worship, or submission before someone, often rendered as prostrating oneself.
Of structures, cities, or kingdoms falling into ruin or being destroyed, as in the prophetic declaration that Babylon has fallen.
To fall physically from an elevated position or to drop downward, as objects or persons falling from a height or into a pit.
To fall in a moral or spiritual sense, including stumbling into sin, failing, or falling from a state of grace.
Used imperatively or volitionally for something to fall upon or come upon someone, as in calling for mountains to fall on oneself or lots falling to determine outcome.
